deep.reconstruction:
Notation (from the preceding pages): ∫1/z^m = ζ(m) = Σ_z z^{-m}, and ∫(1/z^m)(1/y^n) = Σ_{z≥1} z^{-m} Σ_{y=1}^{z} y^{-n}. With the diagonal included, this is the non-strict double sum ζ*(m,n) = ζ(m,n) + ζ(m+n), where ζ(m,n) = Σ_{z>y} z^{-m} y^{-n}.

Euler has two methods.
- First method: ζ*(m,n) + ζ*(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n) + ζ(m+n). This is the stuffle (harmonic-product) relation.
- Second method: Σ_{x≠y} x^{-m} y^{-n} = ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) is expanded by partial fractions into sums of the same type of total weight m+n. In effect this is the shuffle/partial-fraction relation.

He sorts everything by the weight m+n.

End of §11 (weight 2). The two methods give 2ζ*(1,1) = ζ(1)² + ζ(2) and 2ζ*(1,1) = ζ(1)² − ζ(2). These look contradictory. Euler waves the difference away: ζ(2) is negligible against the infinite ζ(1)², so nothing can be concluded at weight 2.

§12 (weight 3, m=2, n=1).
- The partial-fraction expansion of ζ(2)ζ(1) − ζ(3) gives 2ζ(2)ζ(1) − ζ*(2,1) − 2ζ(2)ζ(1) + ζ*(1,2) + ζ*(2,1), which collapses to ζ*(1,2). So ζ(2)ζ(1) − ζ(3) = ζ*(1,2).
- The first method gives ζ*(2,1) + ζ*(1,2) = ζ(2)ζ(1) + ζ(3).
- Subtracting, the divergent pieces cancel: ζ*(2,1) = 2ζ(3), i.e. Σ_{n≥1} H_n/n² = 2ζ(3), equivalently strict ζ(2,1) = ζ(3).

Euler stresses that the result is true, and will be confirmed later. He also says one cannot trust it on this derivation alone, because divergent quantities were manipulated. He explicitly flags the identity 1 + (1/2²)(1+1/2) + (1/3²)(1+1/2+1/3) + … = 2(1 + 1/2³ + 1/3³ + …) as worthy of all attention.

The problem served is the evaluation of linear Euler sums (double zeta values) in closed form, order by order in the weight.
errors: Not an error but a gap: the derivation subtracts two equations that each contain the divergent ζ(1). Euler himself says it is not rigorous; he gets the value right (Σ H_n/n² = 2ζ(3) is correct) and promises independent confirmation.

At weight 2 (end of §11, top of this page) the two methods really are inconsistent by a finite amount (ζ(2) versus −ζ(2)). Dismissing this as 'vanishing relative to infinity' is not valid as a finite statement. In modern terms the discrepancy is the genuine mismatch between shuffle- and stuffle-regularised values of ζ(1,1).
Typographical: the first displayed series omits a final '+ etc.' on the left-hand side.

ideas.modern_name: Euler's evaluation of the linear Euler sum / the duality ζ(2,1) = ζ(3)
ideas.where_published: E477, Novi Comm. Acad. Petrop. 20 (1776); also Euler–Goldbach letters

ideas.what: Combining the product (stuffle) relation with the partial-fraction (shuffle-type) expansion of ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) to get linear relations among double sums of fixed weight
ideas.modern_name: Double shuffle relations for double zeta values
ideas.usually_credited_to: Modern formulation: Hoffman, Ihara–Kaneko–Zagier (2006); origin commonly traced to Euler E477

ideas.what: Formal cancellation of divergent ζ(1) terms between the two relations
ideas.modern_name: Regularised double shuffle (formal regularisation of ζ(1) = T)

ideas.what: Grading the problem by the weight m+n
ideas.modern_name: Weight filtration of multiple zeta values

missed.claim: The finite discrepancy Euler meets at weight 2 (2ζ*(1,1) = ζ(1)² + ζ(2) from one method, ζ(1)² − ζ(2) from the other) is precisely the kind of finite correction that Ihara–Kaneko–Zagier's comparison map between shuffle- and stuffle-regularisations accounts for. It is not a negligible quantity. Euler encountered the first instance of this phenomenon and dismissed it. Historical accounts usually credit E477 with the double-shuffle idea, but I am unsure whether anyone has pointed out that Euler's discarded weight-2 'contradiction' is the regularisation defect.
missed.quote: verum cum ∫1/z sit infinita, eius respectu vtique pars altera ∫1/z² pro euanescente est habenda. Quam ob causam hinc nihil ad institutum nostrum concludere licet.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical anchor for the regularisation theorem in MZV theory. It shows that naive cancellation of infinities works at weight 3 but provably fails at weight 2 unless corrected.

deep.surprise_reason: The main result, Σ H_n/n² = 2ζ(3), is famous and credited to Euler, and E477 is widely recognised as the origin of double-shuffle-type relations. The only mildly interesting point is reading Euler's dismissed weight-2 inconsistency as the shuffle/stuffle regularisation defect, which may or may not already be remarked in the literature.
transcription_corrections: First displayed series should end with '+ etc' before '= 2∫1/z³' (it is truncated in both print and transcription).
In the decomposition line, '+1∫1/z²(1/y)' is '+ ∫1/z²(1/y)' with coefficient 1; the printed '1' is a plain coefficient, not a stray symbol.
'vnico modo' (§12) is correct as printed; 'iteram' in the print is a misprint for 'iterum'.
